searchText: <@881905303011086387> for the capella types, how is the type determined: 1. LightClientBootstrap via header.becon.slot 2. LightClientUpdate via attestedHeader.beacon.slot or signatureSlot 3. LightClientFinalityUpdate via attestedHeader.beacon.slot or signatureSlot 4. LightClientOptimisticUpdate via attestedHeader.beacon.slot or signatureSlot ? another problem on fork boundaries, for lets say LightClientUpdate/LightClientFinalityUpdate, where attestedHeader is capella but finalizedHeader is bellatrix should the update be skipped in case the headers + signature slot don't lie in the same epoch? Hey <@792822129019584562>, in that case, the `finalized_header` will need need to be upgraded using the function `upgrade_lc_update_to_capella` or `upgrade_lc_header_to_capella` before processing it. This is described in the `fork.md` document contained in: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/capella/light-client/fork.md ok similar thing on the deneb fork boundary? before processing you mean before forming the LightClientUpdate object? Question really is can LightClientUpdate has different fork objects for attested and finalized? Yeah that has also been described for `eip4844`: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/eip4844/light-client/fork.md processing part is understood thanks 👍 , to form and transmit these objects,(LightClientUpdate/FinalityUpdate) finalizedHeader should also be upgraded then right? which basically leads to this question as well So I think before processing any of the type of updates (either `LightClientUpdate`, `LightFinalityUpdate`, or `LightClientOptimisticUpdate`) they would need to supplied to the relevant upgrader functions before processing the data. In the pyspec tests, the data contained an additional field called `update_fork_digest` which allowed me to detect which fork type it belongs by recomputing the forkversion. However, I am not sure this data is available through the light client API or over p2p. and when building (even before some store could process them) can LightClientUpdate.attestedHeader LightClientUpdate.finalizedHeader be of different forks if they are for e.g. separated by fork boundary? for ssz based objects to be read, 1. I am not sure if the fork context is available over p2p 2. what determines the fork of lightclientupdate/finality update: signature slot, attested header slot, or finalized slot 3. I am assuming for the ssz objects to be read/written in clean and simple manner: fork of the update will also be fork of the attestedheader/finalizedheader and the objects will need to be upgraded to the same fork if they are of lesser forks at the time object is being build/assembled my expectation for which i need confirmation: for 1. if its not, it should be made available for 2 it should be signature slot as its/would be the most ahead for 3. yes all should be same fork object Correct me if I am wrong here <@881905303011086387> , however, according to the specs for full nodes to generate light client data, the function `block_to_light_client_header` is extended for each fork (Capella and Deneb) to allow them to generate the object appropriate to the epoch that corresponds to the `SignedBeaconBlock`. For Capella, the function `block_to_light_client_header` is extended to: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/eip4844/light-client/full-node.md the up-gradation path for header is clear and not the source of confusion, but the update's fork and its (attested/finalized) header's fork <@881905303011086387> does this assumption sound reasonable? On (1), it is `header.beacon.slot`. On (2) – (4), it is `attested_header.beacon.slot`. https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/altair/light-client/p2p-interface.md This is documented here, e.g.,: > The gossip ForkDigest-context is determined based on compute_fork_version(compute_epoch_at_slot(finality_update.attested_header.beacon.slot)). Yes, that can happen, and is covered in pytests. You can have updates with finalized in fork A, attested in fork B, and signature in fork C. The `attested_header.slot` determines the overall spec fork that you use for generating the `LightClientXyzUpdate`. `create_light_client_update` calls that spec fork's `block_to_light_client_header` for both the attested and finalized header. The upgrade thing is on the client side, when you have a local `LightClientStore` from a later fork, and want to consume existing data based on earlier forks. for 1: – libp2p Gossip: the Fork Digest is part of the gossip Topic name string. – libp2p Req/Resp: the Fork Digest context is sent as a prefix: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/altair/p2p-interface.md#forkdigest-context – REST SSZ: the Fork Digest is derivable from `Eth-Consensus-Version` HTTP header, in all responses. For `LightClientUpdate` array, it is interleaved with the data. – REST JSON: the Fork Digest is derivable from various `version` properties for 2: – always attested header slot. this is the canonical format exchanged over the network for 3: – yes, it is always consistent. If your `LightClientStore` is from a later fork, you can use the `upgrade` helpers to convert older data to be processable with latest `LightClientStore`. Yes, `attested_header.slot` determines the update's fork. While generating the update, you use the `block_to_light_client_header` from that fork, for both attested/finalized updates. ok sounds good! thanks <@881905303011086387> and <@624875260373762069> 🙂 🙏 It would be very appreciated if you could submit a PR to `ethereum/consensus-specs` to improve clarity, btw. sounds good 🙂, will PR shortly for the same will pick/copy paste from the above clarifications 😆 Capella just hit on the public Zhejiang testnet! 🎉

excerpts.author: etan_status
excerpts.content:
On (1), it is `header.beacon.slot`.
On (2) – (4), it is `attested_header.beacon.slot`.
https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/altair/light-client/p2p-interface.md
This is documented here, e.g.,:
> The gossip ForkDigest-context is determined based on compute_fork_version(compute_epoch_at_slot(finality_update.attested_header.beacon.slot)).

excerpts.author: etan_status
excerpts.content: Yes, that can happen, and is covered in pytests. You can have updates with finalized in fork A, attested in fork B, and signature in fork C.

excerpts.author: etan_status
excerpts.content:
The `attested_header.slot` determines the overall spec fork that you use for generating the `LightClientXyzUpdate`.
`create_light_client_update` calls that spec fork's `block_to_light_client_header` for both the attested and finalized header.

The upgrade thing is on the client side, when you have a local `LightClientStore` from a later fork, and want to consume existing data based on earlier forks.

excerpts.author: etan_status
etan_status
excerpts.content: Yes, `attested_header.slot` determines the update's fork. While generating the update, you use the `block_to_light_client_header` from that fork, for both attested/finalized updates.
